title: Exact bit complexity of the variable-dimension tilt-DP dual
statement: Determine whether min_beta v_K(S_psi-beta S_lambda), with K and d_lambda part of the rational input, admits exact algebraic optimization in polynomial bit complexity using the fixed-tilt interval-DP oracle, including active tie refinements, without materializing a potentially large parametric-DP envelope. Settled by DS-TILT-DUAL-CERTIFICATE and its audit: fixed-tilt exact evaluation, polynomial certified-epsilon minimization, exact polynomial-bit minimization at d_lambda=1 for every K (root-separation bisection), and exact minimization in polynomially many arithmetic operations for fixed d_lambda>=2 with variable K (Toledo 1993 fixed-dimension parametric search with degree-2 comparisons). Remaining: a polynomial bit bound for fixed d_lambda>=2 with variable K (a root-separation argument for the conic breakpoint arrangement carried through the parametric search), and any exact statement, or hardness obstruction, for variable d_lambda.
assumptions: positive rational weights; exact-K nonempty cells; rational score table
exact means an algebraic optimizer/value with checkable comparisons, not a crossings grid or epsilon approximation
common empirical nuisance-null directions may be quotiented before optimization
the d_lambda=1 case is closed by AUDIT-DS-PRACTICAL-CERTIFIED-SOLVER section 7.5; the fixed-d_lambda arithmetic bound is prior art (Toledo 1993), not a bit bound

proof_location.section: OP31. Exact bit complexity of the tilt-DP dual

warning: General parametric-shortest-path envelope lower bounds do not automatically transfer to the special scalar grouping DP, and Megiddo/Toledo parametric search shows the envelope need not be materialized. A valid hardness reduction for variable d_lambda, or a bit-complexity analysis of fixed-dimension parametric search, is required.
